title: What’s your least painful way to clean up a dense AI mesh for real-time use?
author: SomewhereAny5899
selftext:
I’ve been trying to work out a more practical cleanup path for AI-generated props before bringing them into a game engine.

The options I keep coming across are decimate in blender, running the model through instant meshes, or using something like meshy’s remesh before exporting. They all seem workable, but not without different tradeoffs. Decimate looks like the quickest option for static props, while remeshing may give you something easier to edit at the cost of losing some smaller details.

I’m mostly working with environment props, so I’m not looking for perfect topology or something that needs to deform. I just want the model to keep its shape, look right in-engine, and not turn into another long cleanup job.

anyone using generated assets in an actual project, what’s your least painful way to clean up a dense AI mesh for real-time use?

comments.author: SomewhereAny5899
comments.body: For a bit more context, these are mostly background props.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body: Auto topology tools. Go to r/TopologyAI and browse for an while, you will see some great solutions.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I'm about to try again but last month I tried and my answer was I should just rebuild it myself, the model I tried to repair just made it more clear it wasn't ready yet

replies.author: SomewhereAny5899
replies.body: Feel you and that’s exactly the outcome I’m trying to avoid lol.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: yeah but as I was putting in the work trying to fix everything wrong with the model, I found myself getting much more comfortable with using blender in general. if I was looking to do a specific thing most of the time I could use AI to explain it (I used claude for my project but any general question I used google because its free. and now I feel like I actually can just do the model myself and use AI to make it even easier.

comments.author: kaisarehman
comments.body: Try autoremesh latest version from github. Its very good. I use it to remesh high rez ai generated model with it. Then i used paw bakery to bake normal map on the low rez mesh. So far happy with the result. Its not perfect but good.

replies.author: SomewhereAny5899
replies.body:
This actually makes me think I may be looking at the tradeoff the wrong way? Instead of choosing between using meshy’s remesh and keeping the smaller surface details, I could keep the dense model as the bake source and use the remeshed version as the low-poly target.

But I’m still unsure about whether that scales past one prop. Did you have to redo the uvs and cage setup for each mesh, or does paws bakery automate enough of that to make it practical for a whole set of background props?

replies.author: kaisarehman
replies.body:
I have used paw bakery for single object baking so far and it easy and work nicely. In my case i did not use Cage was the meshes was pretty much aligned and without cage the textures baked nicely. and for the UVs the objects are not animated so I mostly use smart UVs and island packing. 

some time the remeshed version needs fixing, i notice some open hole or overlaping faces. so i take some time to clean it.
